The concept of a **Quality Indicator Target** (referred to in the source documents as *udviklingsmål*, or developmental goal) establishes the specific performance thresholds that healthcare providers are expected to meet or exceed for various clinical quality indicators. These targets are essential for benchmarking clinical performance, ensuring patient safety, and driving continuous quality improvement within the healthcare system. 

Across the documented framework, targets are assigned to a range of specific indicators, each tailored to the nature of the metric being measured. For indicators where high compliance or success rates are expected, the targets are set at 80% or above. For example, [[indikator-3|Indikator 3]] and [[indikator-4b|Indikator 4b]] have the most stringent targets, requiring a performance level of ≥ 95% [^src1]. Similarly, [[indikator-1|Indikator 1]] and [[indikator-4a|Indikator 4a]] are held to a standard of ≥ 90% [^src1]. [[indikator-2|Indikator 2]] has a target of ≥ 80%, while [[indikator-8|Indikator 8]] has a lower threshold, aiming for ≥ 50% [^src1].

Conversely, for indicators that track adverse events, complications, or negative outcomes, the targets are designed to keep the incidence rate as low as possible. [[indikator-5|Indikator 5]] has a strict upper limit, with a target of ≤ 0.8% [^src1]. This specific target for Indikator 5 is reinforced in multiple sections of the reporting guidelines [^src2]. Furthermore, [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]] mandates an even lower threshold, with a developmental goal of ≤ 0.6% [^src1]. 

Together, these targets form a comprehensive scorecard for evaluating clinical quality, balancing the pursuit of high adherence in positive care processes with the minimization of risks in adverse outcomes.
